result.title: LoCo: Selective Local Competition for Discriminative Open-Vocabulary Multi-Label Recognition
result.comment: The paper is accepted by NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Open-Vocabulary Multi-Label Recognition (OV-MLR) aims to identify all queried semantic concepts present in an image. Existing methods mainly improve global image-text matching or text-side representations, leaving local prediction largely under-explored. In this paper, we revisit local prediction and reveal that it can serve as a strong discriminative branch once two properties are properly handled: spatial consistency of local visual features and compatibility-aware local competition. This perspective is motivated by local semantic sparsity: each image region is related to only a small subset of queried concepts, while compatible concepts of different granularities or types may still coexist locally. We instantiate this perspective with LoCo, a selective Local Competition framework for OV-MLR. LoCo adopts a spatially consistent visual encoder to reduce local feature entanglement, and introduces Selective Softmax to impose competition only among locally incompatible categories while preserving compatible responses. Multi-scale inference further improves local prediction at different scales. LoCo can also be ensembled with an existing global predictor to provide complementary image-level context. Experiments on four multi-label benchmarks show that standalone LoCo improves average F1-score and mAP over TagCLIP by 3.4% and 3.8%, respectively. LoCo + DualPrompt achieves the highest averages among the compared methods, with gains of 4.8% and 5.2% over TagCLIP. Our results suggest that local semantic sparsity offers a useful basis for developing more discriminative open-vocabulary multi-label recognition methods. The code is available at https://github.com/lee-plus-plus/LoCo.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向开放词表多标签识别，重新审视局部预测分支，提出 LoCo：用空间一致的视觉编码器减轻局部特征纠缠，并以 Selective Softmax 只在局部互斥概念间施加竞争、保留兼容响应，配合多尺度推理与全局预测器集成，在四个基准上提升 F1 与 mAP。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「局部语义稀疏性」假设与按区域只激活少量相关概念的筛选机制，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与候选假设竞争提供可核查线索，但论文本身不做推理状态生成或答案使用分析，联系需人工判断。
